from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are displacements, like (x, y).",
            "Basis vectors i-hat and j-hat build space.",
            "Any point is a combination of these."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, [1.5, 1, 0], buff=0, color=GOLD)
        label_v = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE).next_to(vector.get_end(), UP)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 4], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        self.play(Create(vector), Write(label_v))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        i_hat = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color=BLUE)
        j_hat = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP, color=RED)
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=BLUE).next_to(i_hat.get_end(), DOWN)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=RED).next_to(j_hat.get_end(), LEFT)
        
        self.play(Create(i_hat), Create(j_hat), Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 1.5), color=WHITE)
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scale vectors and add them together.",
            "The span is the set of all reach.",
            "Different directions span the whole plane."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations & Span", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize Mobjects
        v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color="#00FF00")
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP, color="#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(v1, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(v2, 'C4')
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        
        v_sum = Vector(v1.get_vector() + v2.get_vector(), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(VGroup(v1.copy(), v2.copy()), v_sum))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        span_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area_custom(span_rect, 'D3', 'E4')
        self.play(FadeIn(span_rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.5}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.wait(2)

    def place_in_area_custom(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Dependence means one vector is redundant.",
            "Redundant vectors don't increase your reach.",
            "Co-linear vectors are linearly dependent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: Redundancy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Vectors
        # Collinear vectors
        v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, color=BLUE)
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, color=ORANGE)
        
        # Group them
        vectors = VGroup(v1, v2)
        self.place_at_grid(vectors, 'C2')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(v2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(v1.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A basis must span the entire space. [Asset: SpanningSet]",
            "A basis must be linearly independent. [Asset: IndependentSet]",
            "Every point has one unique representation. [Asset: UniqueCoord]"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Bases: The Perfect Coordinate System", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements

        grid_lines = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1], color="#808080", background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#808080", "stroke_width": 1})

        dot = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        point_pos = 2*RIGHT + 1*UP
        dot.move_to(grid_lines.c2p(2, 1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), Create(basis_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#808080"), Create(grid_lines))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Create(dot))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", [

            "Independence is your efficiency.",
            "A basis is your optimal coordinate system."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        span_obj = Text("Span", color="#FFFF00")
        indep_obj = Text("Independence", color="#FFFF00")
        basis_obj = Text("Basis", color="#FFFF00")
        
        matrix_summary = Matrix([[1, 0], [0, 1]], color="#00BFFF")
        example_app = Text("Camera Perspective", color="#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.place_at_grid(indep_obj, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(basis_obj, 'B6')
        self.play(FadeIn(span_obj), FadeIn(indep_obj), FadeIn(basis_obj))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display a transformation matrix summary
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_summary, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_summary))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # Show a final example vector application
        self.place_at_grid(example_app, 'F3')
        self.play(FadeIn(example_app))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vector Spaces: Span, Independence, and Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
sections.content: Briefly define a vector as an ordered pair (x, y) representing displacement. Introduce the 'Grid' visualization where basis vectors i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1) act as the building blocks for any point in 2D space.
sections.example: Imagine a robot on a 2D floor; any move is a combination of horizontal (i) and vertical (j) steps.

sections.title: Linear Combinations & Span
sections.content: Define linear combination: c1*v1 + c2*v2. Explain 'Span' as the set of all reachable points. Visualize this as the 'area of influence' created by scaling and adding vectors.
sections.example: If you have two vectors pointing in different directions, their 'Span' is the entire 2D plane. If they point the same way, the 'Span' is just a single line.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: Redundancy
sections.content: Explain that a set is linearly dependent if one vector can be formed by the others (it provides no new 'reach'). Visualize this as two vectors lying on the same line or three vectors in a flat 2D plane.
sections.example: If you have a robot that can move North (N) and East (E), adding a third vector 'Northeast' (N+E) is redundant—it's a 'dependent' movement that doesn't increase reach.

sections.title: Bases: The Perfect Coordinate System
sections.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that are (1) Linearly Independent and (2) Span the entire space. It is the minimal set of vectors needed to describe every point uniquely.
sections.example: Using standard grid vectors (1,0) and (0,1) as a basis for a map. Any location can be described by exactly one combination of these two units.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Recap: Span (reach), Independence (efficiency), and Basis (the skeleton). Connect these to data science—where variables are vectors and a 'basis' represents the most efficient way to store information.
sections.example: In a 3D video game engine, the 'basis' defines the camera's orientation. Changing the basis allows the engine to calculate perspectives from any character's viewpoint.
